subject: VPC pricing breakout, migration credits and ops/support banding
messages:
From: Jake Morales <jake.morales@opshealth.com>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@opshealth.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: VPC commercial questions and price breakout

Priya —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to follow up with a couple of clarifying questions so we can finalize the commercial term sheet:

1) Platform fee amortization: Our finance team needs the math showing how the platform fee would be amortized against a 12‑month committed GPU pool. Is that a calendar pro‑rata or billed monthly based on committed units? Also, if we scale up mid‑term, how do credits/proration work?

2) Migration / transition credit: You mentioned a migration credit for customers moving from hosted to VPC. Can you confirm the rules (how many months, is it applied to platform fee only or to consumption as well)?

3) Support tiers: We want to split dev/non‑prod support from production oncall. Can support hours be pooled across environments and how is oncall priced for a 24x7 Platinum SLA?

I've attached our internal SOW draft (OpsHealth_SOW_R1.pdf) with expected environments and ramp schedule.

Goal: get a clean commercial approval by end of this week so legal can start redlines.

—Jake
Head of IT Ops, OpsHealth

From: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
To: Jake Morales <jake.morales@opshealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC commercial questions and price breakout

Jake —

Thanks for the clear list. Below are concrete answers and a couple of options so your finance/procurement can pick the best fit. I've attached a quick price CSV and a draft SOW (RI_SOW_draft_v1.docx) that reflects option B below.

1) Platform fee amortization
- Default: calendar monthly billing based on committed capacity (USD/month). Platform fee is invoiced monthly, but customers can elect annual prepay which gives a 2.5% discount.
- Mid‑term scale ups: additional committed units are prorated for the remainder of the term (calculated on a days‑remaining basis) and billed on the next monthly invoice. Example math included in Pricing_Tiers_20260616.csv.

2) Migration credit (hosted -> VPC)
- Standard: one‑time credit equal to 2 months of average hosted spend, applied as a credit against the platform fee invoices.
- Alternative (for larger deals): up to 3 months credit if customer commits >= 12 months and a minimum committed GPU pool (we typically set threshold at 4x baseline).
- Credit applies against platform fee and can also be applied to consumption invoices at customer request (we prefer platform fee first).

3) Support tier split and oncall
- Support is structured by tier: Silver (business hours), Gold (extended hours + 4‑hour P1), Platinum (24x7 + dedicated SE + quarterly ops review).
- Support hours can be pooled across environments under a single Platinum engagement — price is a function of number of oncall seats and severity coverage. For OpsHealth sizing, Gold -> Platinum uplift is detailed in the CSV; Platinum includes 1 dedicated oncall seat + escalation to oncall team.

Options for you to consider (summary):
A) Metered + monthly platform fee: lower up‑front, migration credit = 2 months, typical for customers who prefer flex.
B) Committed annual prepay + larger credit: 2.5% prepay discount + up to 3 months migration credit, guaranteed capacity nodes and faster SLA lead times (recommended for production critical).

Next steps: if you want, Ben can run the exact numbers against your SOW and produce a redline for procurement. If OpsHealth prefers option B, we can prepare a DocuSign-ready SOW + term sheet today.

I'll schedule a quick sync with Ben and Marissa for Thursday 10am PT unless you prefer a different time.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Principal Commercial Manager, Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555‑0183

From: Jake Morales <jake.morales@opshealth.com>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@opshealth.com
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC commercial questions and price breakout

Priya —

Appreciate the clear options. A few follow ups from procurement after reviewing the CSV:

- OpsHealth is leaning to option B (annual prepay) but we need 4 months migration credit, not 3. Can you stretch to 4 months if we sign a 24‑month commit? Our finance teams are sensitive to migration lift.

- Proration question: if we downscale committed units mid‑term (rare but possible), is there any clawback? We need a cap on negative adjustments to protect us.

- Support: can the dedicated SE be made part‑time for the first 3 months (to reduce cost) and then convert to full‑time upon production cutover? We'd like pricing that supports a stepped SE commitment.

If you can confirm the 4 months credit on a 24‑month commit and provide language for a capped downscale adjustment (e.g., up to 25% of committed capacity eligible for pro‑rata refunds), we can push legal to move quickly.

—Jake

From: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
To: Jake Morales <jake.morales@opshealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC commercial questions and price breakout

Jake —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the pragmatic asks. Internal alignment below (Ben/Marissa/Vivek looped). Proposed commercial positions we can take to legal:

1) Migration credit: approve 4 months credit on a 24‑month committed contract. We will apply the credit first to platform fee; customer can elect to reassign to consumption invoices via the SOW.

2) Downscale/clawback cap: accept a capped adjustment for downscales with the following guardrails — customer can downscale up to 25% of committed capacity once per 12‑month window with pro‑rata credit, additional downscales will be subject to a 50% early‑reduction fee on the delta. We'll surface the exact formula in the SOW examples.

3) SE ramp (stepped): agree to a stepped SE schedule — 0.5 FTE for first 3 months at a reduced uplift rate, moving to 1.0 FTE at production cutover. We'll add a line item and conversion schedule in the SOW.

4) Timeline / SOW delivery: Ben will produce a redline and a DocuSign package today if OpsHealth confirms option B + 24 months. Marissa will update the SOW to include the downscale examples and stepped SE pricing. Expect delivery by end of day Friday.

Action items:
- Jake: confirm Option B + 24 months commitment and acceptance of the four‑month migration credit by EOD Monday.
- Ben: produce DocuSign package and redline SOW (target: Fri EOD).
- Marissa: add pricing examples for downscale and SE ramp to the SOW.

If that matches procurement's needs, we can get this to legal and aim for signature within two weeks.

Best regards,
Priya Natarajan
Principal Commercial Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: RI_SOW_draft_v1.docx, Pricing_Tiers_20260616.csv
